examples.japanese: {宗教|しゅうきょう}{儀礼|ぎれい}に{参加|さんか}した。
examples.english: I participated in a religious ceremony.

examples.japanese: {通過|つうか}{儀礼|ぎれい}は{文化|ぶんか}によって{異|こと}なる。
examples.english: Rites of passage differ depending on the culture.

examples.japanese: {古代|こだい}の{儀礼|ぎれい}が{現代|げんだい}まで{受|う}け{継|つ}がれている{地域|ちいき}もある。
examples.english: In some regions, ancient rituals have been passed down to the present day.

examples.japanese: {儀礼|ぎれい}{的|てき}な{挨拶|あいさつ}を{交|か}わした。
{外交|がいこう}では{儀礼|ぎれい}を{重|おも}んじることが{大切|たいせつ}だ。
examples.english: In diplomacy, it is important to respect etiquette.

examples.japanese: {儀礼|ぎれい}{的|てき}な{訪問|ほうもん}だったが、{実|じつ}は{重要|じゅうよう}な{話|はなし}もあった。
examples.english: It was a courtesy visit, but there was actually important business to discuss.

notes:
Has two related but distinct uses. In sense 1, it refers to formal ceremonies and rituals, especially religious or cultural ones. In sense 2, it means polite formality or protocol observed in social and diplomatic interactions.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {宗教|しゅうきょう}{儀礼|ぎれい}: religious ceremony
- {通過|つうか}{儀礼|ぎれい}: rite of passage
- {儀礼|ぎれい}{的|てき}な: ceremonial, formal, perfunctory
- {儀礼|ぎれい}{訪問|ほうもん}: courtesy visit

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {礼儀|れいぎ}: manners, politeness — everyday personal conduct
- {式典|しきてん}: ceremony — a specific formal event
- {儀式|ぎしき}: ceremony, ritual — largely synonymous with sense 1, but more focused on the structured procedure
